issues.legal_issue: A concluded land-ceiling proceeding may be reopened after a long delay where the governing power sets no time limit, provided the affected landholder receives notice and an opportunity to be heard.
material_facts: An earlier land-ceiling proceeding had been dropped after the authorities found no surplus land, and the State did not challenge that decision through the available appeal, revision, or review processes.
About fourteen years later, the Collector issued a show-cause notice proposing to reopen the proceeding because land transfers had allegedly been improperly excluded.
The landholders replied to the notice and were heard before the proceeding was reopened and the surplus land was determined.
issues.conclusion: The delay did not invalidate the reopening because no time limit was prescribed, and the landholders were given notice and an opportunity to be heard.
issues.legal_principle: Section 45-B of the Bihar Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling Area and Acquisition of Surplus Land) Act, 1961 empowered the State Government or the authorized Collector to call for and examine a disposed proceeding and direct its reopening and fresh disposal. In the absence of a prescribed time limit, reopening was not invalid merely because of delay, but the affected person had to be afforded an opportunity by show-cause notice. No earlier cases were cited on this issue.

rule.if: land_ceiling_proceeding and earlier_proceeding_concluded and reopening_authority_found_reason_to_reexamine and no_fixed_reopening_deadline and affected_holder_received_notice_and_hearing

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: The authorities were determining the land a landholder could retain and whether any land was surplus.
predicates.earlier_proceeding_concluded: The earlier proceeding had been disposed of and its decision had not been challenged through the available review processes.
predicates.reopening_authority_found_reason_to_reex: The reopening authority identified a reason to examine the earlier disposal again.
predicates.no_fixed_reopening_deadline: The governing reopening power prescribed no time limit for exercising it.
predicates.affected_holder_received_notice_and_hear: The authority gave the affected landholder notice of the proposed action and an opportunity to respond before deciding.

issues.definition: When a concluded land-ceiling proceeding is reopened for an identified reason under a power with no fixed deadline, reopening after delay is permitted if the affected landholder receives notice and a hearing.

issues.legal_issue: Land conveyed after the statutory cutoff remains subject to the ceiling calculation even when it had previously been mortgaged and possession had been given to the mortgagee, and the conveyed land is treated as selected by the landholder for retention within the ceiling limit.
material_facts: Landholders had mortgaged land and given possession to the mortgagees before the statutory cutoff date.
Registered sale deeds conveying the land to the mortgagees were executed after the cutoff date, and title passed under those deeds.
The sales were made without prior written permission, and the authorities included the land in the ceiling calculation when determining surplus land.
issues.conclusion: The earlier mortgages did not make the land a pre-cutoff transfer; because the sale deeds conveying title were executed after the cutoff, the transferred land was to be treated as selected by the landholders for retention within their ceiling limits.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9(2) of the Bihar Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling Area and Acquisition of Surplus Land) Act, 1961 treats land transferred in accordance with or in contravention of Section 5(1)(ii) as selected by the landholder for retention within the admissible ceiling area. The Court treated the mortgage as not transferring title before the cutoff, because title passed only under the later sale deeds. Section 2(g), which defines a landholder, was also considered. No earlier cases were cited on this issue.

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: The authorities were determining a landholder's permissible retention and surplus land.
predicates.landholder_had_mortgaged_land_before_cut: The landholder had mortgaged the land and given possession to the mortgagee before the applicable cutoff.
predicates.title_conveyance_occurred_after_cutoff: A later conveyance transferred title to the land after the applicable cutoff.

issues.definition: In a land-ceiling proceeding, land mortgaged before the cutoff but conveyed by a later transfer of title is treated as selected by the landholder for retention within the ceiling limit.
